scenario: Two humanitarian nutrition programmes, NutriA and NutriB, are evaluated on recovery rates across severely and moderately malnourished children. NutriA operates predominantly in severely malnourished populations; NutriB mostly serves moderate cases.

data.description: Recovery success rates by malnutrition severity

question: (a) Which programme has the higher aggregate recovery rate? (b) Which programme outperforms within each severity class? (c) Compute corrected rates using a 50/50 severity mix.

ground_truth.explanation: NutriB's higher overall rate is driven by its lighter patient load. When severity mix is equalised, NutriA achieves better outcomes in both strata.

naive_answer: NutriB is more effective; its overall recovery rate 0.8906 beats NutriA's 0.7635.
naive_trap: Malnutrition severity is a powerful confounder: NutriA treats 88% severe cases while NutriB treats 88% moderate cases.
reasoning_trace: Severe: A 0.74 > B 0.67. Moderate: A 0.94 > B 0.92. Corrected: A=0.84, B=0.795. A wins.
python_verification:
nAs,rAs,nAm,rAm = 750,0.74,100,0.94
nBs,rBs,nBm,rBm = 100,0.67,750,0.92
ovA=(nAs*rAs+nAm*rAm)/(nAs+nAm); ovB=(nBs*rBs+nBm*rBm)/(nBs+nBm)
assert ovB > ovA
cA=0.5*rAs+0.5*rAm; cB=0.5*rBs+0.5*rBm
assert abs(cA-0.84)<0.005 and abs(cB-0.795)<0.005
assert cA > cB
